en.greeting: Hi! You already know my bag and Rina's phone. Today we'll learn mine, yours and theirs, ask Whose …? and write 's and s' the right way. Let's go step by step.

steps.title: my bag → mine
steps.text: In Indonesian you can say 'Tas ini punya saya'. English needs a special word for that.
steps.body: **my, your, his, her, our, their** always need a thing right after them: **my bag**. When we don't say the thing again, we use **mine, yours, his, hers, ours, theirs** with **nothing after**: *This bag is **mine***. Not 'This bag is my': **my** can't end a sentence. **his** doesn't change. No apostrophe: **yours, hers** (not 'your's').

steps.title: In real sentences
steps.text: Look: nothing comes after mine, yours, his, hers or theirs.
steps.body: *Mine is black* = my umbrella is black. **yours** is for one person and for a group (kamu / kalian). Careful who is talking: Budi and Sari say 'It's **ours**', but you say about them 'It's **theirs**'.

examples.en: That umbrella isn't mine. Mine is black.
examples.id: Payung itu bukan punya saya. Punya saya hitam.

examples.en: Is this coffee yours, Bu Ani?
examples.id: Kopi ini punya Ibu, Bu Ani?

examples.en: Our office is small, but theirs is big.
examples.id: Kantor kami kecil, tapi kantor mereka besar.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: At the office, a colleague holds up a phone charger. It belongs to you.

question.prompt: Is this your charger? — Yes, it's ___.
question.explanation: Nothing comes after the word (the charger is already clear), so we use **mine**. **my** needs a thing after it (my charger), and **mines** doesn't exist here.

steps.title: Build the sentence
steps.text: You and your family have a white car. Someone thinks the red one is yours.

question.prompt: Arrange the words: Mobil merah itu bukan punya kami.
question.explanation: **punya kami** with no thing after it = **ours**. The describing word comes before the thing (**red car**), and **ours** ends the sentence: **That red car isn't ours.**

steps.title: Whose …?
steps.text: Now let's ask about the owner, for one thing or many.
steps.body: One thing: **Whose + thing + is this?** More than one (plural): **Whose + things + are these?** Answer with a name + 's or with **mine, yours, his, hers…**: *It's Rina's.* / *They're his.* For many things, start with **They're**. **who's** sounds the same but means **who is**: *Who's that man?* Trick: if 'who is' fits the gap, write **who's**.

steps.title: Ask about the owner
steps.text: After prayers at the musholla, there are many shoes at the door. You want to know who they belong to.

question.explanation: We ask about the owner, so **whose**. **Shoes** is more than one, so **are these**: **Whose shoes are these?** 'Who's' means 'who is', and 'is this' is for one thing.

steps.title: 's or s'?
steps.text: Last part: one owner or more than one?
steps.body: **One owner**: add **'s** → *my sister's room*. **More than one**, and the word already ends in s: add only **'** → *my parents' house* (mother and father). **More than one** but no s at the end (*children, people, men, women*): add **'s** → *the children's toys*. The owner comes first: **my friend's book**, not 'the book of my friend' (*buku teman saya*). You can't hear the difference; only the writing shows it.

pairs.id: rumah orang tua saya (ayah dan ibu)

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: Rina has two brothers. They share one bedroom. Rina shows you the door.

question.explanation: Two brothers = more than one owner, and **brothers** already ends in s, so add only **'**: **my brothers' room**. **brother's** means only one brother, and **brothers** without ' doesn't show the owner.

steps.title: Build the sentence
steps.text: Your friend's kids share a bedroom. It's not very big.

question.prompt: Arrange the words: Kamar anak-anak kecil.
question.explanation: The owners come first: **children** is more than one but doesn't end in s, so it takes **'s**: **the children's room**. Then **is small**.

steps.title: Quick review
steps.text: Flip the cards to remember the forms.

id.greeting: Hai! Kamu sudah tahu my bag dan Rina's phone. Hari ini kita belajar mine, yours dan theirs, bertanya Whose …?, dan menulis 's dan s' dengan benar. Yuk, pelan-pelan saja.

steps.title: my bag → mine
steps.text: Dalam bahasa Indonesia kamu bisa bilang 'Tas ini punya saya'. Bahasa Inggris butuh kata khusus untuk itu.
steps.body: **my, your, his, her, our, their** selalu harus langsung diikuti benda: **my bag**. Kalau bendanya tidak disebut lagi, pakai **mine, yours, his, hers, ours, theirs** **tanpa kata sesudahnya**: *This bag is **mine***. Bukan 'This bag is my': **my** tidak bisa jadi akhir kalimat. **his** tidak berubah. Tanpa apostrof: **yours, hers** (bukan 'your's').

steps.title: Dalam kalimat nyata
steps.text: Perhatikan: tidak ada kata sesudah mine, yours, his, hers atau theirs.
steps.body: *Mine is black* = payung saya hitam. **yours** dipakai untuk satu orang dan untuk banyak orang (kamu / kalian). Perhatikan siapa yang bicara: Budi dan Sari bilang 'It's **ours**' (punya kami), tapi kamu bilang tentang mereka 'It's **theirs**' (punya mereka).

examples.en: That umbrella isn't mine. Mine is black.
examples.id: Payung itu bukan punya saya. Punya saya hitam.

examples.en: Is this coffee yours, Bu Ani?
examples.id: Kopi ini punya Ibu, Bu Ani?

examples.en: Our office is small, but theirs is big.
examples.id: Kantor kami kecil, tapi kantor mereka besar.

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Di kantor, rekan kerjamu mengangkat sebuah charger HP. Itu punyamu.

question.prompt: Lengkapi: Is this your charger? — Yes, it's ___.
question.explanation: Tidak ada kata sesudahnya (chargernya sudah jelas), jadi kita pakai **mine**. **my** harus diikuti benda (my charger), dan **mines** tidak dipakai di sini.

steps.title: Susun kalimatnya
steps.text: Kamu dan keluargamu punya mobil putih. Ada yang mengira mobil merah itu punya kalian.

question.prompt: Susun kata-katanya: Mobil merah itu bukan punya kami.
question.explanation: **punya kami** tanpa benda sesudahnya = **ours**. Kata sifat ada sebelum bendanya (**red car**), dan **ours** ada di akhir kalimat: **That red car isn't ours.**

steps.title: Whose …?
steps.text: Sekarang kita bertanya tentang pemiliknya, untuk satu benda atau banyak.
steps.body: Satu benda: **Whose + benda + is this?** Lebih dari satu (jamak): **Whose + benda + are these?** Jawab dengan nama + 's atau dengan **mine, yours, his, hers…**: *It's Rina's.* / *They're his.* Untuk banyak benda, awali dengan **They're**. **who's** bunyinya sama tapi artinya **who is**: *Who's that man?* Trik: kalau 'who is' cocok di tempat kosong, tulis **who's**.

steps.title: Tanyakan pemiliknya
steps.text: Selesai salat di musala, ada banyak sepatu di depan pintu. Kamu ingin tahu sepatu itu punya siapa.

question.explanation: Kita menanyakan pemiliknya, jadi **whose**. **Shoes** lebih dari satu, jadi **are these**: **Whose shoes are these?** 'Who's' artinya 'who is', dan 'is this' untuk satu benda.

steps.title: 's atau s'?
steps.text: Bagian terakhir: pemiliknya satu atau lebih dari satu?
steps.body: **Satu pemilik**: tambahkan **'s** → *my sister's room*. **Lebih dari satu**, dan katanya sudah berakhiran s: tambahkan **'** saja → *my parents' house* (ayah dan ibu). **Lebih dari satu** tapi tidak berakhiran s (*children, people, men, women*): tambahkan **'s** → *the children's toys*. Pemilik di depan: **my friend's book**, bukan 'the book of my friend' (*buku teman saya*). Bedanya tidak terdengar; hanya tulisannya yang menunjukkan.

pairs.id: rumah orang tua saya (ayah dan ibu)

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Rina punya dua saudara laki-laki. Mereka tidur di satu kamar. Rina menunjukkan pintunya kepadamu.

question.explanation: Dua saudara = pemiliknya lebih dari satu, dan **brothers** sudah berakhiran s, jadi tambahkan **'** saja: **my brothers' room**. **brother's** artinya hanya satu saudara, dan **brothers** tanpa ' tidak menunjukkan pemilik.

steps.title: Susun kalimatnya
steps.text: Anak-anak temanmu tidur di satu kamar. Kamarnya tidak terlalu besar.

question.explanation: Pemiliknya di depan: **children** artinya lebih dari satu tapi tidak berakhiran s, jadi pakai **'s**: **the children's room**. Lalu **is small**.

steps.title: Ulangan cepat
steps.text: Balik kartunya untuk mengingat bentuk-bentuknya.
